scope: HTTP asset client cookie authentication, immutable upload inputs, complete operation deadlines and response cleanup
coverage: Exact HTTPS origin, browser-only cookies, rejected mixed credentials and immutable configuration.
Multipart bytes and explicit scope for course content, assessment submissions and chat attachments.
Bearer cookie omission, invalid inputs rejected before authentication and no mutation during pending credentials.
Redacted authentication failures without retry or fallback.
Mock-time stalled credential, fetch, stream and non-stream deadlines; late-response cancellation and stream cleanup.
Real loopback HTTP multipart success and 307 redirect rejection without forwarding file or bearer token.
limitations: Cookie transport assertions use an injected browser origin and fetch; they do not establish real browser cookie delivery or deployed SSO acceptance.
The real HTTP test uses synthetic data and bearer authentication on a development loopback server, not a production asset backend.
The reference asset server route, scoped retrieval, durable storage/idempotency, scanning and retention remain unimplemented.
Deadline expiry cannot prove server rollback or stop underlying custom credential/transport work that ignores cancellation.
RSS is sampled process-group memory for these checks, not a whole-system measurement, long-running load test or leak-free guarantee.
No live issuer, native-device trial, paid provider request, deployment or institution acceptance was performed; production gates remain open.
